defect.description: The edge case where new_mobject is old_mobject: the new deduplication removes the object from the list before searching, so scene.replace(a, a) no longer finds a, raises ValueError and leaves a removed from the scene; the deduplication must skip the case new_m is old_m (or run only after the replacement).
defect.location: src/scene.py (the deduplication at the top of replace_in_list)

review_items: src/scene.py:37 replace(m, m) raises ValueError because dedup removes object before search
src/scene.py:38 remove(new_m) drops only first occurrence of duplicates
tests/test_scene.py:34 single-element assertion can't verify order preservation
tests/test_scene.py:43 same single-element group assertion concern
votes.evidence_quote: `replace(m, m)` raises `ValueError` instead of being a no-op — `mobj_list.remove(new_m)` removes the object before the search loop at line 43 can find it, so line 51 raises
votes.justification: The review's first finding names the exact defect: the dedup at the top of replace_in_list removes new_m when it is the same object as old_m, so the search fails and ValueError is raised. It also proposes the right guard (skip when new_m is old_m).
